item.title: Patterson et al. 2026 Heavy Summer Rain Days and Next-Year Oak Acorn Crops. Ecological Indicators
item.itunes:title: Patterson et al. 2026 Heavy Summer Rain Days and Next-Year Oak Acorn Crops. Ecological Indicators
item.description:
At Bent Creek Experimental Forest, the heaviest 10 percent of early-summer rain days tracked next year's chestnut and white oak acorn crops; light rain showed no link. For white oak they explained about three quarters of variation.
Source article: Infrequent, high-volume rainfall events modulate acorn production for two common oak species in Western North Carolina, USA. Patterson et al., Ecological Indicators, 2026. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecolind.2026.115726
This summary was generated by AI and read by a synthetic voice, for educational purposes only. It may contain errors or omissions. Consult the original article before relying on it.

item.title: Way 2006 Herbert Stoddard and the Case for Fire in Longleaf. Environmental History
item.itunes:title: Way 2006 Herbert Stoddard and the Case for Fire in Longleaf. Environmental History

item.title: Patrick et al. 2022 Resistance Versus Resilience After Storms. Science Advances
item.itunes:title: Patrick et al. 2022 Resistance Versus Resilience After Storms. Science Advances
item.description:
A synthesis of more than 4,000 coastal monitoring time series from 26 tropical cyclones, mostly estuaries and offshore waters. Ecosystems that resist storm change tend to recover slowly, and those that change more recover faster.
Source article: A general pattern of trade-offs between ecosystem resistance and resilience to tropical cyclones. Patrick et al., Science Advances, 2022. https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abl9155

item.title: Maurer et al. 2013 Wind Tracks Forest Growth. Agric. For. Meteorol.
item.itunes:title: Maurer et al. 2013 Wind Tracks Forest Growth. Agric. For. Meteorol.

item.title: Delaporte et al. 2022 Cyclone Winds and Forest Recovery. Remote Sensing
item.itunes:title: Delaporte et al. 2022 Cyclone Winds and Forest Recovery. Remote Sensing

item.title: Klotzbach et al. 2022 Late Season Caribbean Hurricanes. Bull. Am. Meteorol. Soc.
item.itunes:title: Klotzbach et al. 2022 Late Season Caribbean Hurricanes. Bull. Am. Meteorol. Soc.
item.description:
Covers the October–November 2020 Atlantic hurricane finish, with five major hurricanes driven by low wind shear and warm western Caribbean water. A simple summer model using the ENSO longitude index and Atlantic warm pool would have predicted the surge.

item.title: Carney et al. 2024 Informal Trade Behind Wiregrass Restoration. Trees, Forests and People
item.itunes:title: Carney et al. 2024 Informal Trade Behind Wiregrass Restoration. Trees, Forests and People
item.description:
Interviews with 20 Florida landowners, land managers, and conservation staff show wiregrass restoration runs on trust-based swaps of seed, burn crews, and equipment. Seed costs about $1,700 per pound, and goodwill, more than profit, drives the sharing.
Source article: The informal economy of wiregrass production for longleaf pine restoration in Florida. Carney et al., Trees, Forests and People, 2024. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tfp.2024.100620
This summary was generated by AI and read by a synthetic voice, for educational purposes only. It may contain errors or omissions. Consult the original article before relying on it.
